Save what looks good.
Order what works for everyone.

Ordering together is as easy as eating together.

SAVD · Careem Food product challenge · prototype with mock data
The problem

One person ends up running lunch.

🎬 A colleague drops a food reel in WhatsApp.
Everyone: “Let’s try that.”
Then I find the restaurant, collect every order, place it and chase the money.
What breaksReels get saved to remember a place. When the group finally decides, nobody can find the saves.
Who pays the priceThe host. They organise, advance the money and still eat last.
SAVD lets the host start lunch and take part like everyone else.

When things go wrong

Every problem has a visible next step.

Missed cutoffHost extends 10 minutes or continues with ready members.

Fees changeAffected people reconfirm. The host never silently covers a share.

Payment failsBasket stays. Retry, or the host proceeds without them.

Also built: unmatched reel (Find the restaurant), featured dish sold out (browse the rest of the menu), branch can’t deliver (another branch or restaurant).
Features

What the prototype does today.

Groups

Create or join

Join with a code or link. See the group name and delivery location before joining.

Saves

Private by default

Paste a reel, confirm the restaurant and dish. Sharing with the group is a separate tap.

Decide

Find our lunch

One pick, two alternatives, and a plain reason. Delivery, diet and budget are checked for everyone.

Start

Host confirms once

One branch, one address, one cutoff. The card becomes Join lunch order.

Order

Own basket, exact share

Choosing and Ready states. Items plus an even share of delivery and service fees. One order, one status.

Safety

Five hard cases

Unmatched reel, sold-out dish, branch can’t deliver, missed cutoff, failed payment.

Business opportunity

Turn a reel in a chat into a Careem Food order.

Capture the moment

People discover food in reels, then decide in a group chat. Today that intent ends as a screenshot. SAVD keeps it inside the app.

Bigger, repeat baskets

A group orders together, so more meals go out per delivery. Office lunch repeats every week.

New users through invites

A group order needs the whole team. Invited colleagues join through a link.

Demand signal for restaurants

Counts of saves by dish and area show partners what people want before they order.

Beachhead: office groups in dense areas such as Downtown, DIFC and Business Bay. Revenue: existing order and delivery fees and restaurant commission, with clearly labelled promoted spots only later. These are hypotheses the pilot tests, not measured results.
Outcomes

What changes for the group, the host and Careem.

The group

Decides faster

One recommendation with a reason. Nobody is left without a meal they can eat.

The host

Eats like everyone

No collecting orders, no chasing money, no covering for others.

Careem

More orders from reels

Higher reel-to-order conversion, larger group baskets, repeat office lunches and new users from invites.

Measured by: time from reel shared to order placed · host interventions · people left without a suitable meal · share of groups that complete an order. Guardrails: late deliveries, failed payments, wrong-order reports.
How we validate it

Same reel, same group of three. Two ways to decide.

A · Today’s flow

  • Careem group order
  • Shortlist by price and distance
  • Host collects choices and chases payments

B · SAVD

  • Saves and group fit pick the restaurant
  • Everyone adds a meal and confirms a share
  • Host places one order

What we measure

  • Time from sharing the reel to placing the order
  • Host interventions (chasing, fixing, covering)
  • People left without a suitable meal

The assumption to test

A saved reel shows curiosity, not a plan. Start with reels members share or mark Want to try. Then test whether ordinary bookmarks improve the pick.

Early pass: 4 of 5 groups reach a choice with nobody left out.

Launch smart

Start small, inside one office, with what people choose to share.

Phase 1 · Office Lunch

  • One area, a few office groups
  • Shared reels and Want to try only
  • Fees split evenly, simulated first

Phase 2 · Learn taste

  • Save is curious, “I’d order this” is interested, reorder is liked
  • Users can correct what SAVD thinks

What production needs

  • Reel metadata: platform links and previews, with user-pasted links as the base case
  • Restaurant and menu matching to Careem Food listings

 

  • Delivery coverage by branch and address
  • Payments: per-person authorization, one captured order, partial refunds if a share changes

Before we decide, save it.
When we decide, order it together.

Next: run 5 office groups through A and B this week, compare time, interventions and who got left out, then fix what repeats.
